events.title: Rider Advocate brief: 5 claims (0 void)
events.body:
C1: The trip ran 12.4 km against a 10.8 km optimal route, +1.6 km (+15%), and GPS isolates one off-route segment at 14:19–14:22 that added 0.77 km while straying up to 1019 m off the optimal route — an unexplained deviation from the shortest and most direct route. [F1 F3] [RD-1]
C2: The deviation is not excused by traffic: no traffic incident was recorded near the route during the trip window, and the only speed-band records (Ayer Rajah Expressway and Central Expressway, band 4 / 30–39 km/h) are not incidents and are not severe congestion (band 1 or 2), so RD-4(a) and (b) give the driver no justification. [F9 F10 F11] [RD-4]
C3: The rider never agreed to the reroute: there are no in-app chat messages at all in this trip, so there is no rider message sent before 14:19 consenting to the segment; the driver's post-trip statement that 'I followed my GPS; it rerouted me' is a statement made after the segment and is not consent. [F7 F8] [RD-5]
C4: The fare was a fixed RydeX quote (surge 1.0x) billed on the optimal 10.8 km distance — base $3.90 + distance $15.17 + time $4.50 + platform $1.47 = $25.04 — with no waiting fee and no off-tariff add-on, so under RD-2 there is no metered excess to refund and the recoverable amount for the 0.77 km off-route segment is the disclosed distance component rather than the whole fare. [F4 F5 F6] [RD-2]
C5: This is not an isolated lapse: the driver has 2 route disputes upheld in the last 90 days, this case being at least the third, which under the 90-day 'repeated' standard warrants referring the driver's account to Ryde for review alongside the refund. [F14] [RD-6]
Weaknesses: Because RydeX is a fixed-price service, RD-2's non-metered branch refunds only unpublished add-ons; the fare facts show the billed distance (10.8 km) does not exceed the optimal route and there is no waiting fee, no toll/ERP item and no extra charge (F4, F5, F6), so the refund sized on the 0.77 km detour may be considered nominal rather than the 'extra distance' the complaint asks for. | The off-route segment added only 0.77 km within a total +1.6 km excess, and the remaining +0.83 km was not attributed to any off-route segment (F1, F3) — the driver can argue the residual is map-matching noise below the 0.2 km tolerance per segment and that the trip took 18.9 min against a 17 min estimate (F2). | The driver has a strong profile of his own — 5.8 years, 4.8 rating, 851 trips in 90 days (F14) — which he will use to argue a single GPS reroute is not a pattern of overcharging; but the same fact shows 2 route disputes upheld in 90 days, supporting our C5.
Asks: refund_partial $1.12

claims.assertion: The trip ran 12.4 km against a 10.8 km optimal route, +1.6 km (+15%), and GPS isolates one off-route segment at 14:19–14:22 that added 0.77 km while straying up to 1019 m off the optimal route — an unexplained deviation from the shortest and most direct route.

The deviation is not excused by traffic: no traffic incident was recorded near the route during the trip window, and the only speed-band records (Ayer Rajah Expressway and Central Expressway, band 4 / 30–39 km/h) are not incidents and are not severe congestion (band 1 or 2), so RD-4(a) and (b) give the driver no justification.

The rider never agreed to the reroute: there are no in-app chat messages at all in this trip, so there is no rider message sent before 14:19 consenting to the segment; the driver's post-trip statement that 'I followed my GPS; it rerouted me' is a statement made after the segment and is not consent.

The fare was a fixed RydeX quote (surge 1.0x) billed on the optimal 10.8 km distance — base $3.90 + distance $15.17 + time $4.50 + platform $1.47 = $25.04 — with no waiting fee and no off-tariff add-on, so under RD-2 there is no metered excess to refund and the recoverable amount for the 0.77 km off-route segment is the disclosed distance component rather than the whole fare.

This is not an isolated lapse: the driver has 2 route disputes upheld in the last 90 days, this case being at least the third, which under the 90-day 'repeated' standard warrants referring the driver's account to Ryde for review alongside the refund.

weaknesses: Because RydeX is a fixed-price service, RD-2's non-metered branch refunds only unpublished add-ons; the fare facts show the billed distance (10.8 km) does not exceed the optimal route and there is no waiting fee, no toll/ERP item and no extra charge (F4, F5, F6), so the refund sized on the 0.77 km detour may be considered nominal rather than the 'extra distance' the complaint asks for.

The off-route segment added only 0.77 km within a total +1.6 km excess, and the remaining +0.83 km was not attributed to any off-route segment (F1, F3) — the driver can argue the residual is map-matching noise below the 0.2 km tolerance per segment and that the trip took 18.9 min against a 17 min estimate (F2).

The driver has a strong profile of his own — 5.8 years, 4.8 rating, 851 trips in 90 days (F14) — which he will use to argue a single GPS reroute is not a pattern of overcharging; but the same fact shows 2 route disputes upheld in 90 days, supporting our C5.

claims.assertion: This is a non-metered RydeX trip: the fare was quoted as a fixed price at booking, so distance driven during the trip does not change what the rider pays (F6 shows the total $25.04 with distance billed at exactly 10.8 km).
The billed distance (10.8 km, distance component $15.17) does not exceed the optimal route distance of 10.8 km, so there is no excess distance inside the charged fare to refund (F4, F6).

The GPS record shows a single 0.77 km off-route segment (14:19–14:22, 2.15 km driven vs 1.38 km optimal, max 1019 m from the optimal route), and the driver's position was within 200 m of the optimal route for the remainder of the trip (F3, F1).
The whole trip's extra travel time is only 1.6 minutes (18.9 min vs 17 min estimated), which is inconsistent with the rider's claim of a fare inflated by a deliberate detour (F2).

No congestion was recorded on the optimal route: the only speed bands are band 4 (30–39 km/h) on AYE and CTE, no traffic incidents were recorded near the route, and weather was fair with 0.0 mm rain, so the driver cannot rely on an RD-4 justified-reroute exemption (F9, F10, F11, F12).

There is no in-app chat at all in this trip, so the driver cannot show a rider message agreeing to a route change before the 14:19 segment started; the driver's statement 'I followed my GPS; it rerouted me' is not consent (F7, F8).

Because the trip is non-metered, the only refundable item on the 0.77 km off-route segment would be any ERP/toll or unpublished post-trip add-on incurred on that segment; the fare breakdown contains no toll or unpublished add-on (F6).
Driver profile shows 851 trips in 90 days and a 4.8 rating, and the two prior upheld route disputes are the only blemish; the rider's two disputes in 90 days were both not upheld (F14, F13).

weaknesses: The GPS record does establish the factual basis of an unexcused deviation: F3 shows a 0.77 km off-route segment between 14:19 and 14:22 with no exemption, so RD-1 is breached and the judge will record a route-deviation violation even if the refund is nil.
F7 shows zero in-app chat, so the driver cannot prove the rider agreed to the route change before it was taken, and F8's 'I followed my GPS' is a claim, not consent (RD-5, G11).

Driver profile F14 shows route_disputes_upheld_90d = 2, which meets the RD-6 threshold (≥ 1 before this case) and makes this a 'repeated' route deviation, exposing the driver to an additional flag_account referral if the judge finds the deviation upheld.

The rider's complaint (and F1's +1.6 km / +15%) overstates the case — but the judge may read the mismatch between the quoted 10.8 km estimate and the 12.4 km actual track as evidence the driver drove further than necessary, even though none of the extra distance was billed (F4).

events.title: Proposed ruling: no_action (model confidence 0.90)
events.body:
Safety screen first: the only rider text is the complaint (app-estimate vs route taken, "he never asked me"), the only driver text is F8 ("I followed my GPS; it rerouted me. Nothing wrong with the fare"), and F7 records no in-app chat at all. Nothing in any of these is a threat, insult, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation; the fare argument is not abuse under SAFE-1. safety_concern = none, safety_basis = [F7][F8], so I may rule on the merits [SAFE-1].

Route: F3 isolates one off-route segment 14:19–14:22, 2.15 km driven against 1.38 km optimal, +0.77 km and up to 1019 m from the optimal route, which is a deviation from the "shortest and most direct route" duty [F3][RD-1]. what_would_change: F3: if the judge finds the rider agreed to this route or named this stop beforehand, it is exempt; if not, $0.00 is refunded; if the record cannot settle it, a person decides.

claims.assertion: The trip ran 12.4 km against a 10.8 km optimal route, +1.6 km (+15%), and GPS isolates one off-route segment at 14:19–14:22 that added 0.77 km while straying up to 1019 m off the optimal route — an unexplained deviation from the shortest and most direct route.

The deviation is not excused by traffic: no traffic incident was recorded near the route during the trip window, and the only speed-band records (Ayer Rajah Expressway and Central Expressway, band 4 / 30–39 km/h) are not incidents and are not severe congestion (band 1 or 2), so RD-4(a) and (b) give the driver no justification.

The rider never agreed to the reroute: there are no in-app chat messages at all in this trip, so there is no rider message sent before 14:19 consenting to the segment; the driver's post-trip statement that 'I followed my GPS; it rerouted me' is a statement made after the segment and is not consent.

The fare was a fixed RydeX quote (surge 1.0x) billed on the optimal 10.8 km distance — base $3.90 + distance $15.17 + time $4.50 + platform $1.47 = $25.04 — with no waiting fee and no off-tariff add-on, so under RD-2 there is no metered excess to refund and the recoverable amount for the 0.77 km off-route segment is the disclosed distance component rather than the whole fare.

This is not an isolated lapse: the driver has 2 route disputes upheld in the last 90 days, this case being at least the third, which under the 90-day 'repeated' standard warrants referring the driver's account to Ryde for review alongside the refund.

weaknesses: Because RydeX is a fixed-price service, RD-2's non-metered branch refunds only unpublished add-ons; the fare facts show the billed distance (10.8 km) does not exceed the optimal route and there is no waiting fee, no toll/ERP item and no extra charge (F4, F5, F6), so the refund sized on the 0.77 km detour may be considered nominal rather than the 'extra distance' the complaint asks for.

The off-route segment added only 0.77 km within a total +1.6 km excess, and the remaining +0.83 km was not attributed to any off-route segment (F1, F3) — the driver can argue the residual is map-matching noise below the 0.2 km tolerance per segment and that the trip took 18.9 min against a 17 min estimate (F2).

The driver has a strong profile of his own — 5.8 years, 4.8 rating, 851 trips in 90 days (F14) — which he will use to argue a single GPS reroute is not a pattern of overcharging; but the same fact shows 2 route disputes upheld in 90 days, supporting our C5.

claims.assertion: This is a non-metered RydeX trip: the fare was quoted as a fixed price at booking, so distance driven during the trip does not change what the rider pays (F6 shows the total $25.04 with distance billed at exactly 10.8 km).
The billed distance (10.8 km, distance component $15.17) does not exceed the optimal route distance of 10.8 km, so there is no excess distance inside the charged fare to refund (F4, F6).

The GPS record shows a single 0.77 km off-route segment (14:19–14:22, 2.15 km driven vs 1.38 km optimal, max 1019 m from the optimal route), and the driver's position was within 200 m of the optimal route for the remainder of the trip (F3, F1).
The whole trip's extra travel time is only 1.6 minutes (18.9 min vs 17 min estimated), which is inconsistent with the rider's claim of a fare inflated by a deliberate detour (F2).

No congestion was recorded on the optimal route: the only speed bands are band 4 (30–39 km/h) on AYE and CTE, no traffic incidents were recorded near the route, and weather was fair with 0.0 mm rain, so the driver cannot rely on an RD-4 justified-reroute exemption (F9, F10, F11, F12).

There is no in-app chat at all in this trip, so the driver cannot show a rider message agreeing to a route change before the 14:19 segment started; the driver's statement 'I followed my GPS; it rerouted me' is not consent (F7, F8).

Because the trip is non-metered, the only refundable item on the 0.77 km off-route segment would be any ERP/toll or unpublished post-trip add-on incurred on that segment; the fare breakdown contains no toll or unpublished add-on (F6).
Driver profile shows 851 trips in 90 days and a 4.8 rating, and the two prior upheld route disputes are the only blemish; the rider's two disputes in 90 days were both not upheld (F14, F13).

weaknesses: The GPS record does establish the factual basis of an unexcused deviation: F3 shows a 0.77 km off-route segment between 14:19 and 14:22 with no exemption, so RD-1 is breached and the judge will record a route-deviation violation even if the refund is nil.
F7 shows zero in-app chat, so the driver cannot prove the rider agreed to the route change before it was taken, and F8's 'I followed my GPS' is a claim, not consent (RD-5, G11).

Driver profile F14 shows route_disputes_upheld_90d = 2, which meets the RD-6 threshold (≥ 1 before this case) and makes this a 'repeated' route deviation, exposing the driver to an additional flag_account referral if the judge finds the deviation upheld.

The rider's complaint (and F1's +1.6 km / +15%) overstates the case — but the judge may read the mismatch between the quoted 10.8 km estimate and the 12.4 km actual track as evidence the driver drove further than necessary, even though none of the extra distance was billed (F4).

points.response: Conceded as to the fare mechanism — RydeX is fixed-price and F6 bills distance at exactly 10.8 km — but RD-2's non-metered branch is not the whole of RD-1: a fixed fare does not license a route that strays up to 1019 m off the optimal route (F1, F3).

True as far as the charged distance goes (F4, F6), but the driver drove 12.4 km on a 10.8 km optimal route (F1) and RD-1's duty is the shortest and most direct route, breached on the record regardless of billing — my C4 already sizes the recovery on the unbilled 0.77 km segment, not on billed excess.

This claim concedes the core of my case: F3 shows a 0.77 km off-route segment at 14:19–14:22 far off the optimal route, and nothing in F1 or F3 supplies any exemption for it, so RD-1 is breached and that segment is an unexempted detour.
A 1.6-minute and 1.6 km excess (F1, F2) does not make the deviation lawful; RD-1 sets no de-minimis or percentage threshold, so a 0.77 km unexempted off-route segment breaches the duty on its own.

I agree there is no RD-4 exemption — that is my own C2: band 4 on AYE and CTE (F9, F10) is neither an incident nor severe congestion, no incident was recorded (F11) and weather was fair (F12), so the deviation stands unexcused.
Accepted: with zero in-app chat (F7) and only a post-trip statement (F8), there is no rider message sent before 14:19 consenting to the segment, so RD-5 grants no exemption.

The absence of toll and add-on items (F6) limits the money on the table but does not reset the case: the 0.77 km off-route segment is the recoverable distance under RD-2, and even at zero dollars the judge must record the RD-1 violation, which feeds the RD-6 referral.

F14 is against the driver, not for him: route_disputes_upheld_90d = 2 satisfies RD-6's threshold of at least one already-upheld route dispute, making this deviation repeated and justifying the flag_account referral; the rider's record (F13) is cited only to show no flag is sought against the rider.

Conceded on the facts: F3 shows one 0.77 km off-route segment at 14:19–14:22 with no exemption, so the RD-1 breach is recorded — but the unreached +0.83 km of F1 is not any off-route segment and the whole trip overran the estimate by only 1.6 minutes (F2), so this is a single GPS-induced deviation, not a fare-inflating detour.

Accepted: no incident was recorded near the route and the only bands are band 4, which under RD-4(b) alone is not severe congestion, so the driver claims no exemption on that basis (F9, F10, F11, F12).

Conceded: F7 shows the chat record contains no in-app messages at all, so there is no consent message timestamped before the 14:19 segment start, and the driver's own post-trip statement (F8) cannot supply it under RD-5.

This claim defeats the rider's own request: on the non-metered branch of RD-2 the only recoverable items are ERP/toll on the off-route segment and any post-trip unpublished add-on, and F6 shows no toll/ERP line and zero waiting fee, so the refund is $0.00 – the rider's own 'disclosed distance component' theory has no basis in RD-2 or FARE-1.

The RD-6 threshold for the 90-day window is already met by the two pre-existing upheld route disputes in F14, so this case adds no further 'repeated' finding of its own, and an 851-trip, 4.8-rated, 5.8-year record (F14) shows no overcharging pattern; if the judge records any RD-1 breach the referral is a matter for Ryde's review, not a ground to inflate the refund.

notices.text: We looked into your fare dispute and are closing it with no refund. Your RydeX fare was a fixed all-in quote of $25.04, so it does not change with the distance actually driven, and we found no toll or extra charge added after the trip. That means there is nothing refundable, and the price stands. We did confirm your driver went off the shortest and most direct route during part of the trip, and that has been recorded on the driver's file and referred for review of repeated route deviations. Thanks for flagging it — that report is what lets us act on their record.

We reviewed the route on this trip and found one segment where you went off the shortest and most direct route — about 0.77 km further than needed and well away from the optimal path — with no exemption applying. Your GPS reroute explanation does not override that duty, and there was no rider agreement in the chat. Because this is your second upheld route dispute in 90 days, your account has been referred to Ryde review as a repeated route deviation. The fare itself stands, so no adjustment applies. Going forward, follow the shortest direct route unless a rider agrees otherwise in chat.
